_readme: Drop a new option folder (with spec.json + model) inside its category folder, then add the folder name to that category's options list below. Nothing in index.html / main.css / main.js needs to change.

instructor.text: Welcome to the Thermal Management lab. Every motor and every ESC turns part of the power it handles into I squared R heat. On this bench you will measure how hot they settle, how long they take to get there, and what cooling actually buys you.

The bench is a machined aluminium deck: the motor sits in a clamped mount on the right, the ESC lies on an anti-static mat beside it, and three phase wires join the two. Pick components from the tiles on the left, then use the Environment and Cooling card above Calculations to set ambient temperature, cooling airflow and the Static or Forward airflow mode.

Two viewport chips change what you see. Thermal camera renders the whole bench in false colour from the live temperature field, with a calibration bar down the side. Reality probe opens the winding hotspot readout, so you can see how much hotter the copper is than the case sensor ever reports.

Module 1, Steady-State Temperature Sweep. Press Arm, set a throttle, and wait for the case temperature to settle. The bench logs each settled operating point on its own, so simply sweep the throttle through five or more distinct settings. Plot the settled temperature against current squared and you get a straight line whose slope is the motor resistance times its thermal resistance.

Module 1, Thermal Time Constant. Arm the bench and watch the heating curve climb. Drag the cursor across the graph to the moment it reaches sixty three point two percent of its total rise; that time is tau. Now repeat at a clearly different throttle. The settled temperature will move enormously, and tau will barely budge — because tau is set by the thermal resistance and the mass of metal storing the heat, not by how hard you are driving the motor.

Module 2, ESC Thermal Check. The ESC on the mat dissipates its conduction loss through the MOSFET drain tabs. Run it at full throttle and watch the board against the eighty degree limit. If it trips into the red, drag a heatsink or a thermal pad onto the board, or fit an ESC with a lower on-state resistance, and run it again.

Module 3, Rotor-Wash Cooling. In still air the case can settle dangerously hot, because a hovering motor breathes its own exhaust. Raise the cooling airflow, drag the ducted fan onto the motor, and switch Static to Forward. Watch the required airflow figure and the settled temperature fall as the flow over the case becomes clean instead of recirculated.

Every thermal experiment is complete. You have measured a steady-state locus, a time constant, an ESC survivability margin and the value of forced cooling. The reward component is now unlocked in the Outputs panel.
